definition: An electronic network that moves money between bank and credit union accounts, used for direct deposits and recurring bill payments.
sourceOrganization: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau; Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
verificationNote: The CFPB describes ACH as electronic transfers between banks and credit unions used for paycheck direct deposits and recurring bill debits. The Federal Reserve describes it as a nationwide network for batches of electronic credit and debit transfers. The wording is a plain-language normalization, not a quotation.
scope: V3 supplement. Not part of the 26-term Banking Basics v1.1 legacy record or its 13 clusters.

definition: The amount of money something is valued at, or the amount by which what a person owns is greater than what they owe, as in net worth.
definitionStatus: Owner approved 2026-10-16 (V3 Phase 5); definition describes monetary value, not an investment instrument
sourceOrganization: Investor.gov (U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission); U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
verificationNote: These sources define net worth as assets minus liabilities. Worth on its own has no official definition, so the wording is an explicit plain-language normalization that describes monetary value.
scope: V3 supplement. Not part of the 25-term Investing Basics v1.1 legacy record or its clusters.

definition: An automated teller machine that lets bank customers complete basic transactions such as deposits and withdrawals.
sourceOrganization: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau; Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation
verificationNote: Defines ATM as automated teller machine and describes deposits and withdrawals as basic transactions. Lists deposits, loan payments, cash withdrawals, and transfers among common ATM transactions. Wording approved as written in CAL-0008; not a quotation.
scope: V3 supplement (CAL-0008). Not part of the legacy v1.1 Banking Basics record.

definition: An electronic bank transfer sent through a wire network to a named recipient.
sourceOrganization: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
verificationNote: Defines a wire transfer as an unconditional order to a bank to pay a fixed or determinable amount to a beneficiary through specified networks or bank books. Wording approved as written in CAL-0008; not a quotation.
scope: V3 supplement (CAL-0008). Not part of the legacy v1.1 Banking Basics record.

definition: A scam using deceptive emails or text messages to steal passwords, account numbers, or other personal and financial information.
verificationNote: Explains that scammers use deceptive email or text messages to steal passwords, account numbers, and other sensitive information. Wording approved as written in CAL-0008; not a quotation.
scope: V3 supplement (CAL-0008). Not part of the legacy v1.1 Banking Basics record.

definition: How easily or quickly an investment can be bought or sold without a large effect on its price.
sourceOrganization: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission — Investor.gov
verificationNote: Defines liquidity as how easily or quickly a security can be bought or sold and explains the price impact of low liquidity. Wording approved as written in CAL-0008; not a quotation.
scope: V3 supplement (CAL-0008). Not part of the legacy v1.1 Investing Basics record.

definition: A record of your credit activity and current credit situation, including account and payment information.
verificationNote: Defines a credit report as a statement containing credit activity and current credit situation, including loan payment history and account status. Wording approved as written in CAL-0008; not a quotation.
scope: V3 supplement (CAL-0008). Not part of the 38-term Credit Foundations workbook record.

definition: A common name for a credit reporting company that collects credit information and creates credit reports.
sourceOrganization: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau; Federal Trade Commission
verificationNote: States that credit reporting companies, also called credit bureaus, track credit history and generate credit reports. Identifies Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion as the three nationwide credit bureaus that collect and update report information. Wording approved as written in CAL-0008; not a quotation.
scope: V3 supplement (CAL-0008). Not part of the 38-term Credit Foundations workbook record.

definition: A free protection that restricts access to your credit file to help prevent new accounts from being opened in your name.
verificationNote: Explains that a security freeze restricts prospective-creditor access and can help prevent identity thieves from opening accounts. Wording approved as written in CAL-0008; not a quotation.
scope: V3 supplement (CAL-0008). Not part of the 38-term Credit Foundations workbook record.

definition: A record of how you have used and repaid credit over time.
verificationNote: Defines credit history as a record of credit accounts and payment behavior shown in a credit report. Explains how credit history affects housing, accounts, credit cards, loans, and borrowing costs. Wording approved as written in CAL-0008; not a quotation.
scope: V3 supplement (CAL-0008). Not part of the 38-term Credit Foundations workbook record.
